claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pickup area: GPS puts him within 200 m of the pickup pin from 14:06:40, and his closest approach was 60 m at 14:07:00.

The driver waited long enough: he was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 40 s, and stood stationary at 181 m from the pin from 14:07:20 until the 14:11:20 cancellation, so the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii) is exceeded either way.
The recorded arrival at 14:06:40 preceded cancellation by 4 min 40 s, so the driver did not abandon the pickup prematurely — he cancelled only after the rider failed to appear.

No external cause (roadworks, incident, weather) prevented the pickup, so the only explanation for the non-boarding is the rider's failure to come to the meeting point the driver indicated in chat at 14:07 ("at the side road").

The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore validly charged on the rider-side record and should stand as no_action; the rider's complaint that the driver 'was not at the entrance' is at most a 181 m discrepancy which does not defeat the within-200 m requirement.

weaknesses: F7 directly contradicts the driver's own statement: timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so the 'I'm Here' requirement in NS-1(i) is not proven — and F6 is internally inconsistent with F7 about the tap (14:07:40), which the rider will use to attack the whole arrival premise.

The driver stopped at 181 m from the pin (F3) and never reached the entrance where the rider waited; a judge may read the 200 m radius (a data-layer parameter, G2) as insufficient and treat the driver as not 'at the pick-up location', which under NS-2 would flip the outcome to refund_full.

If NS-1(ii) is treated as failed because the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while not at the pin in the rider's sense (F6 says he was 181 m away at the tap), NS-2's secondary consequence attaches — flag_account for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button — and F18 shows the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, so RD-6-style escalation risk is real.
Chat messages F10–F13 are the driver's own unverified statements; per the system-record-precedence rule they cannot cure the missing 'I'm Here' record in F7.

[F1 F2 F3 F11] [NS-1]

[F7 F6 F3 F2] [NS-1]
→ D3: Elapsed time is not the test — NS-1 requires (i) a press, (ii) presence, and (iii) waiting, all cumulatively; the 14:06:40 'arrival' in F5 is a proximity trigger only and cannot cure the missing press in F7. [F5 F4 F7] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: The absence of incidents/weather (F14, F15, F16) explains nothing here, and the driver's own 14:07 message put him 'at the side road' (F10) while the rider was at the entrance (F11) — a driver-side meeting-point deviation, which is precisely the failure NS-2 covers. [F14 F15 F16 F10 F11] [NS-2]

[F8 F7 F3 F6 F18] [NS-1 NS-2 NS-7]

points.response: Concede the arithmetic but not the conclusion: the 200 m radius in F2/F1 is a data-layer parameter (gap G2), not the policy test, and the driver's genuine nearest point of 60 m at 14:07:00 (F1) is a fleeting pass — he then parked 181 m away (F3), i.e. away from the entrance where the rider was waiting (F11), which is what NS-1 requires him to occupy.

The 3-minute clock in NS-1(iii) only runs after a valid arrival indicator; F7 records no 'I'm Here' press at all, and even on F6's disputed 14:07:40 press the driver was 181 m from the pin, with his stationary period at that distance beginning 14:07:20 (F3), so the time was not spent waiting 'at the pick-up point'.

Elapsed time is not the test — NS-1 requires (i) a press, (ii) presence, and (iii) waiting, all cumulatively; the 14:06:40 'arrival' in F5 is a proximity trigger only and cannot cure the missing press in F7.

The absence of incidents/weather (F14, F15, F16) explains nothing here, and the driver's own 14:07 message put him 'at the side road' (F10) while the rider was at the entrance (F11) — a driver-side meeting-point deviation, which is precisely the failure NS-2 covers.

The fee can only stand if every NS-1 condition holds; since the driver's own claim file fails NS-1(i) on F7 and he was 181 m from the pin when he claims to have pressed (F3, F6), NS-2 requires the $6.61 in F8 to be refunded in full, and I also ask for the account-review flag under NS-2 given his 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18).

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The dispute is a rider-side challenge to a $6.61 cancellation fee charged after the driver cancelled [F4][F8]. Ryde's no-show fee is only payable through NS-0, which routes a driver-cancellation-with-no-show-allegation through NS-1 [F4][NS-0]. NS-1 requires cumulatively: (i) the "I'm Here" press, (ii) GPS presence at the pickup when pressing, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of waiting within the pickup radius [NS-1].

On (i), the record is contradictory: F7 says no press was ever recorded, while F6 logs a tap at 14:07:40. Both are system records, so neither can be discarded in favour of the other, and the driver's own statement [F13] cannot cure the gap [NS-1]. I resolve this by noting that the platform independently recorded arrival at 14:06:40 and the fee was levied on that basis [F5][F4]; the fee is a platform-side record [F8], and NS-1(i) allows the arrival indicator to be either the driver's tap or a platform confirmation [NS-1]. On the execution trace and on F5/F6 the arrival indicator is treated as satisfied, so NS-1(i) does not fail.

On (ii), the only quantity in the record is GPS distance: closest approach 60 m at 14:07:00, and 181 m at the moment of the recorded tap, with continuous presence inside the radius [F1][F6][F2][F3]. NS-1(ii) is expressed as presence "according to GPS data", and the 181 m position is inside the measured radius; the rider's contrary impression — entrance location [F11], driver parked "at the side road" [F10] — is a statement and yields to the GPS record under the system-record rule [NS-1]. On (iii), the driver was stationary at 181 m from 14:07:20 to 14:11:20, a continuous 4 min 0 s, and within the radius cumulatively 4 min 40 s before cancelling [F3][F2][F5], both above the 3:01 threshold [NS-1].

Because all three NS-1 limbs hold, NS-2 is not triggered and the $6.61 stands [NS-1][NS-2][F8]. No add-on fees are in dispute — no surge applied [F9] and no ERP/toll or waiting-fee item appears [F8][FARE-1]. The environmental facts (no incidents, no speed-band records, fair weather) [F14][F15][F16] do not bear on the pickup, since no diversion was alleged [RD-4]. Finally, RD-6 requires the present case to be upheld against the driver before the profile factor can add an account flag [F18][RD-6]; the present case is not upheld, so no flag attaches.

ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; treat the F6/F7 "I'm Here" contradiction as a data-integrity ticket for the GPS/timeline pipeline; no account action against the driver.

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The driver's own timeline is internally contradictory on the mandatory 'I'm Here' step: F7 records driver_pressed_here_at as null (never tapped), while F6 asserts a tap at 14:07:40. On the record as returned, the driver never performed the required 'I'm Here' press, so NS-1(i) fails and the $6.61 cannot stand under NS-1.

Even if the 14:07:40 tap in F6 is taken as real, the driver was 181 m from the pickup point at that moment, not at the pin; the rider's account (F11) and the driver's own message placing himself 'at the side road' (F10) confirm he was not at the stated entrance. The 'within 200 m' reading in F2/F3 is only the data-layer proxy radius (200 m, gap G2), not proof of being at the pick-up location.

The waiting requirement is measured from a valid arrival indicator. The driver only began his stationary hover at 14:07:20 at a point 181 m away (F3) and cancelled at 14:11:20 (F4), i.e. he never waited more than 3 minutes at the pick-up point itself; the recorded arrival at 14:06:40 in F5 is a proximity trigger, not presence at the pin.
Because at least one of NS-1's cumulative conditions fails, NS-2 applies directly: the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's written statement (F13) that he 'pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes' is a user-submitted statement that is contradicted by the system records in F7 and by his own position record in F3/F6, and under the system-record-wins rule it cannot establish NS-1.

Additional action: the driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days (F18), and this case is a further unfulfilled-arrival cancellation, which is the kind of repeated abuse-of-cancellation-button conduct Ryde treats as account-review material.

weaknesses: F2/F3 show the driver spent 4 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m of the pickup and was stationary 4 min 0 s (F3), and F5 says the platform recorded arrival at 14:06:40 with cancellation 4 min 40 s later — the other side will argue NS-1(iii) is met on its face.

F6 affirmatively records a press of 'I'm Here' at 14:07:40, directly contradicting F7's null value; if the judge accepts F6, the 'never pressed' limb of my case falls away and I am left only with the 181 m distance argument (F3/F6), which depends on reading the 200 m figure as a data-layer parameter and not as NS-1(ii).

The rider's own message F11 ('I'm at the entrance, I don't see you') shows the rider was present but did not board within the window, which the driver will use to characterise this as a genuine rider no-show rather than a driver failure to arrive at the pin.
F18 shows the driver's own no-show disputes are upheld 2/2, which helps me on the account-flag point but also lets the driver argue his arrival behaviour has previously been accepted as compliant.

claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pickup area: GPS puts him within 200 m of the pickup pin from 14:06:40, and his closest approach was 60 m at 14:07:00.

The driver waited long enough: he was within 200 m of the pickup for a cumulative 4 min 40 s, and stood stationary at 181 m from the pin from 14:07:20 until the 14:11:20 cancellation, so the 3-minute threshold in NS-1(iii) is exceeded either way.
The recorded arrival at 14:06:40 preceded cancellation by 4 min 40 s, so the driver did not abandon the pickup prematurely — he cancelled only after the rider failed to appear.

No external cause (roadworks, incident, weather) prevented the pickup, so the only explanation for the non-boarding is the rider's failure to come to the meeting point the driver indicated in chat at 14:07 ("at the side road").

The $6.61 cancellation fee is therefore validly charged on the rider-side record and should stand as no_action; the rider's complaint that the driver 'was not at the entrance' is at most a 181 m discrepancy which does not defeat the within-200 m requirement.

weaknesses: F7 directly contradicts the driver's own statement: timeline shows driver_pressed_here_at is null, so the 'I'm Here' requirement in NS-1(i) is not proven — and F6 is internally inconsistent with F7 about the tap (14:07:40), which the rider will use to attack the whole arrival premise.

The driver stopped at 181 m from the pin (F3) and never reached the entrance where the rider waited; a judge may read the 200 m radius (a data-layer parameter, G2) as insufficient and treat the driver as not 'at the pick-up location', which under NS-2 would flip the outcome to refund_full.

If NS-1(ii) is treated as failed because the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while not at the pin in the rider's sense (F6 says he was 181 m away at the tap), NS-2's secondary consequence attaches — flag_account for abuse of the cancellation/waiting button — and F18 shows the driver already has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, so RD-6-style escalation risk is real.
Chat messages F10–F13 are the driver's own unverified statements; per the system-record-precedence rule they cannot cure the missing 'I'm Here' record in F7.

points.response: Concede the arithmetic but not the conclusion: the 200 m radius in F2/F1 is a data-layer parameter (gap G2), not the policy test, and the driver's genuine nearest point of 60 m at 14:07:00 (F1) is a fleeting pass — he then parked 181 m away (F3), i.e. away from the entrance where the rider was waiting (F11), which is what NS-1 requires him to occupy.

The 3-minute clock in NS-1(iii) only runs after a valid arrival indicator; F7 records no 'I'm Here' press at all, and even on F6's disputed 14:07:40 press the driver was 181 m from the pin, with his stationary period at that distance beginning 14:07:20 (F3), so the time was not spent waiting 'at the pick-up point'.

Elapsed time is not the test — NS-1 requires (i) a press, (ii) presence, and (iii) waiting, all cumulatively; the 14:06:40 'arrival' in F5 is a proximity trigger only and cannot cure the missing press in F7.

The absence of incidents/weather (F14, F15, F16) explains nothing here, and the driver's own 14:07 message put him 'at the side road' (F10) while the rider was at the entrance (F11) — a driver-side meeting-point deviation, which is precisely the failure NS-2 covers.

The fee can only stand if every NS-1 condition holds; since the driver's own claim file fails NS-1(i) on F7 and he was 181 m from the pin when he claims to have pressed (F3, F6), NS-2 requires the $6.61 in F8 to be refunded in full, and I also ask for the account-review flag under NS-2 given his 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18).

The 'never pressed' limb rests on F7 alone while F6, the timeline's own entry, affirmatively logs the tap at 14:07:40 and 3 min 40 s inside 200 m after it; the rider cannot accept F7 from that source while discarding F6, and NS-1(i) is satisfied on the corroborated record (F2, F6).

NS-1(ii) is expressed as presence at the pick-up location according to GPS data, and the only measurement in the record is F2/F3 — within 200 m from 14:06:40 with a closest approach of 60 m at 14:07:00 — with the 181 m position still inside that range; the rider's impression in F11 that the driver was not at the entrance is a statement that loses to these GPS facts.

NS-1(iii) is measured by the cumulative time inside 200 m, which F2 puts at 4 min 40 s before cancellation, and F5 confirms the platform recorded arrival at 14:06:40 with the cancellation only 4 min 40 s later — both exceed the 3:01 threshold irrespective of the exact spot at 181 m.
NS-2 only applies if a limb of NS-1 fails, and on the GPS and timeline facts all limbs are met (F2, F5, F6), so the $6.61 recorded in F8 stands and no refund to the rider is due.

The driver's case does not depend on F13: arrival, dwell time and the more-than-3-minute wait are established by the system records F2, F3 and F5, so the attack on the driver's statement does not disturb NS-1.

The 2 upheld no-show disputes in F18 are historical profile facts that cannot decide this case, and the account-review step in RD-6 requires the present case itself to be upheld against the driver, which it is not on F2 and F5; F18 equally shows 1282 trips in 90 d at rating 4.73.
I concede the narrow point that F7 records no 'I'm Here' timestamp, so I do not rest NS-1(i) on the tap alone; the presence and wait limbs remain proven by F2 and F5.

I withdraw the assertion that the rider's failure is the only explanation: F11 shows the rider was at the entrance and did not see the driver, so the record supports a meeting-point gap rather than bad faith.
